feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 5 (outer ±0.06 m, inner ±0.03 m, 12 mm, 0.8 kg) scored 151.9, the best measured. Its s-bend and slalom line losses are 0.0, and the remaining failure is edge drift to about 0.061 m while the tape is still read. Iteration 6 (16 mm footprint) cut oval progress from 0.71 to 0.51 and brought slalom losses back to 0.95, so the footprint is rejected. Iteration 7 (inner ±0.04 m) cut oval progress to 0.22 and raised oval losses to 1.9, so that spacing is rejected and the Integrator's earlier recommendation to retest it is stale. Iterations 3 and 4 also rejected the 0.10 m track and y 0.06 m. This candidate changes only mass, from 0.8 kg to 0.6 kg, which lowers yaw inertia without touching the sensors. If s-bend and slalom max_error falls below 0.061 m or those runs progress further with losses still at 0, keep the lower mass and test the next mass step. If oval progress falls below 0.5, or oval oscillation rises above 0.33 (iteration 5 gave 0.327), mass was too light for the controller, so revert to 0.8 kg. If s-bend and slalom still reach 0.061 m with losses at 0, the controller's edge response is the limit, not the geometry.
requested_changes: Keep the iteration 5 layout and change only mass from 0.8 kg to 0.6 kg. Iteration 5 showed zero s-bend and slalom losses with max_error about 0.061 m, so lower yaw inertia is the one untested lever that leaves the sensors alone. If oval progress falls below 0.5 (iteration 5 gave 0.71), revert mass to 0.8 kg. Iteration 6 showed that losing oval progress costs more than any edge gain, and iteration 5 is the best measured geometry.

Do not retry inner ±0.04 m (iteration 7 oval progress 0.22), sensor_size 0.016 m (iteration 6 oval progress 0.51), wheel_track 0.10 m (iteration 3 oval progress 0.14) or y 0.06 m (iteration 4 oval progress 0.20). Each was rejected by earlier evidence.
